title: Customer Slab Probabilistic Runway — Oct 2026
summary: Working sheet that produces a probabilistic runway (days remaining) for per-contract dedicated GPU slabs. Combines contract slot commitments, observed per-customer utilization distributions, region-specific supply multipliers, and burst budgets to produce P10/P50/P90 runway estimates and recommended allocation actions.
key_assumptions: Slot = 1 x A100-80GB equivalent slot (normalize other GPUs to this)
Observed per-slot utilization distribution uses trailing 30d telemetry (token-hours / slot-hour)
Burst budget allowed up to 1.5x committed slot-hours for enterprise SLAs (policy: negotiated per contract)
Regional supply factor accounts for scheduled maintenance windows and GPU delivery lag: us-west=1.0, eu-west=0.88, ap-south=0.72
Customers with dedicated+private combos treated as independent demand (no cross-surface fallback) unless contract explicitly allows bursting to hosted pool
No additional reserved capacity purchases assumed beyond known signed contracts in spreadsheet; pipeline deals modeled separately in scenario B
methodology: Monte Carlo simulation (10k draws) per contract using historical per-slot utilization distribution + demand growth noise. For each draw we apply regional supply multipliers and per-contract burst allowances, compute remaining slot-hours until the committed slab is exhausted, and convert to runway in days given demand profile. Outputs aggregated percentiles per-contract and global aggregate. Calibration done against last quarter observed outages/overcommit events.
rows_sample: C-1834, VestaSearch, us-west, A100-80GB, 48, 62%, 88%, 720, 1.00, 12, 38, 120, 'monitor + outreach if P10 < 14', moderate
C-1907, FinOptics, eu-west, H100-94GB(normalized 1.12), 96, 74%, 95%, 1440, 0.88, 6, 24, 90, 'propose staggered uplift or reserved burst', high
C-1721, RetailQ, ap-south, A100-80GB, 12, 31%, 65%, 180, 0.72, 40, 120, 360, 'no immediate action', low
percentile_results: Aggregate P50 runway (days) across all signed dedicated contracts: 46
Estimated probability of at least one contract breaching committed SLO in next 30 days: 17%
Median spare slot-hours (after applying burst budgets) across regions: us-west 4.8%, eu-west 2.1%, ap-south -1.6%
allocation_scenarios: Base: current supply, no new reservations. Shows 17% near-term breach probability.
Supply-constrained: simulate 12% reduction in regional supply for eu-west (maintenance bump) - P10 drops by ~6 days for affected contracts.
Demand-surge: 25% sudden uplift for top 5 customers over trailing median — increases probability of breaches to 42% and shifts recommended actions to immediate uplift or contract repricing.
actions: Flag high-risk contracts (P10 < 14 days) and start 2-week escalation: Solutions Eng + Customer Success outreach
Reserve temporary burst pool (48 A100-equivalent hours) in us-west to cover top 3 high-risk customers for 30 days
Eng: schedule targeted capacity activation window in eu-west (eta +18 days) and communicate ETA to impacted customers
Product: evaluate contractual burst-rate charge for new Dedicated customers to disincentivize unbounded bursting
Ops: add nightly check to ingestion pipeline to detect sudden >15% shift in per-slot utilization and re-run simulation automatically
open_questions: Should we include hosted-pool fallback as an explicit option in customer SLAs? Current contracts ambiguous.
How to treat quantized-inference deployments with variable per-token cost — do we map to normalized slot-hours or keep separate?
Can Sales provide expected close dates for pipeline deals C-2012 and C-2025 to include in Scenario C?
Do we have per-contract accepted maintenance blackout windows to adjust regional supply factor more precisely?
notes: Quick notes: initial run used trailing 30d; try 60d to smooth spike noise
